name: Isosorbide dinitrate
className: Organic nitrate (vasodilator used in cardiac disease)

src.q: Each tablet contains diluted isosorbide dinitrate equivalent to 10 mg isosorbide dinitrate.
One tablet contains 30 mg lactose and 80 mg sucrose.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Prophylaxis of angina pectoris; congestive cardiac failure.

src.q: 4.1 Therapeutic indications Prophylaxis of angina pectoris; congestive cardiac failure.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction or brand-specific prescribing statement in the UK SmPC used; no MHRA or SPS advice found for isosorbide dinitrate.

items.t: Adults and elderly: one or two tablets (10-20 mg) three or four times daily.

src.q: Adults and elderly patients One or two tablets taken three or four times daily.

items.t: Safety and efficacy in children not established; no child dose given.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Isosorbide Dinitrate Tablets 10 mg has not yet been established in children.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to isosorbide dinitrate, other nitrates or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance, other nitrates or to any of the excipients.

items.t: PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil): co-administration is contraindicated.

src.q: their co-administration with nitrates or nitric oxide donors is therefore contraindicated

items.t: Acute MI with low filling pressures; acute circulatory failure (shock, vascular collapse); severe hypotension; HOCM; constrictive pericarditis; cardiac tamponade; low cardiac filling pressures; aortic or mitral valve stenosis.

src.q: Acute myocardial infarction with low filling pressures, acute circulatory failure (shock, vascular collapse), severe hypotension, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM), constrictive pericarditis, cardiac tamponade, low cardiac filling pressures, aortic/mitral valve stenosis

items.t: Raised intracranial pressure (e.g. after head trauma, including cerebral haemorrhage); marked anaemia; hypovolaemia.

src.q: disease associated with a raised intra-cranial pressure e.g. following a head trauma and including cerebral haemorrhage, marked anaemia, hypovolaemia.

items.t: Use with caution in hypothyroidism, hypothermia, malnutrition, angle-closure glaucoma, and severe hepatic or renal impairment.

src.q: These tablets should be used with caution in patients who are suffering from hypothyroidism, hypothermia, malnutrition, angle closure glaucoma, severe hepatic or renal impairment.

items.t: Circulatory collapse may follow the first dose, especially with labile circulation; postural hypotension and syncope can occur.

src.q: Symptoms of circulatory collapse may arise after the first dose, particularly in patients with labile circulation.
This product may give rise to symptoms of postural hypotension and syncope in some patients.

items.t: Tolerance and cross-tolerance to other nitrates and nitrites may occur.

src.q: Tolerance and cross-tolerance to other nitrates and nitrites may occur.

items.t: Contains lactose and sucrose: patients with hereditary fructose or galactose intolerance, galactosaemia, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, galactose intolerance, galactosaemia, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil): potentiate the hypotensive effect; may cause life-threatening cardiovascular complications. Contraindicated.

src.q: This might lead to life threatening cardiovascular complications. Concurrent use is contraindicated

items.t: Blood-pressure-lowering medicines (beta-blockers, calcium-channel blockers, vasodilators, angiotensin II receptor antagonists), neuroleptics, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol may increase the hypotensive effect.

src.q: Concurrent intake of drugs with blood pressure lowering properties e.g. betablockers, calcium antagonists, vasodilators, alprostadil, aldesleukin, angiotensin II receptor antagonists etc. and/or alcohol may potentiate the hypotensive effect of the tablets.
This may also occur with neuroleptics and tricyclic antidepressants.

items.t: ACE inhibitors: circulatory collapse can occur in patients already taking them.

src.q: Symptoms of circulatory collapse can arise in patients already taking ACE inhibitors.

items.t: Use with caution in severe renal impairment. No numeric threshold or dose adjustment given.

src.q: severe hepatic or renal impairment

items.t: Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment. No dose adjustment given.

src.q: severe hepatic or renal impairment

items.t: Safety in pregnancy not established. Use only if the physician judges the possible benefits outweigh the hazards. No BUMPS leaflet for nitrates was found.

src.q: Safety in pregnancy has not been established for isosorbide dinitrate.
should only be used in pregnancy and during lactation if, in the opinion of the physician, the possible benefits of treatment outweigh the hazards

items.t: Nitrates pass into breast milk and may cause methaemoglobinaemia in the infant. Use only if benefits outweigh hazards; caution in nursing women. No SPS breastfeeding page for nitrates was found.

src.q: There is data that nitrates are excreted in breast milk and may cause methemoglobinemia in infants.
caution should be exercised when administered to nursing women

items.t: No data on effects on fertility.

src.q: No data on effects of fertility are available.

items.t: Very common: headache (lessens with continued use). Common: hypotension; at the start or after a dose increase, light-headedness on standing, dizziness, drowsiness, reflex tachycardia and weakness. Headache, dizziness, fatigue, palpitations, orthostatic hypotension and flushing may occur at the start and usually settle with a lower dose.

src.q: Very common: headache. The incidence of headache diminishes gradually with time and continued use.
Vascular disorders Common: hypotension.
These symptoms may be associated with dizziness, drowsiness, reflex tachycardia, and a feeling of weakness.
Headache, dizziness, fatigue, palpitations, orthostatic hypotension, and flushing may occur at the beginning of treatment.

items.t: Collapse (sometimes with bradyarrhythmia and syncope); severe hypotension may worsen angina.

src.q: Collapse may occur (sometimes accompanied by bradyarrhythmia and syncope). Severe hypotension may lead to enhanced angina symptoms.

items.t: Very rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, angioedema. Frequency not known: exfoliative dermatitis. Uncommon: allergic skin reaction, sometimes severe.

src.q: Very rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, angioedema
Uncommon: allergic skin reaction (e.g. rash) which may sometimes be severe.

items.t: Temporary hypoxaemia may occur; in coronary artery disease this may lead to myocardial hypoxia.

src.q: Particularly in patients with coronary artery disease this may lead to a myocardial hypoxia.

monitoring.note: No laboratory or routine monitoring stated in the UK SmPC used (emc 10 mg tablets); no SPS monitoring page found for nitrates.
